clue.text: Henry Brooke's deliverance

definitions.meaning: the Irish writer Henry Brooke wrote a long religious poem with this title
being saved or rescued, especially from sin

explanation.definitionFit: Brooke's poem bears this title, and the word means salvation or rescue from sin or evil.

clue.text: Cyril Connolly pool of significance to Eustace and Hilda

definitions.text: Cyril Connolly pool of significance to Eustace and Hilda

parts.words: Cyril Connolly pool of significance to Eustace and Hilda
parts.note: Connolly's only novel is The ___ Pool, and in L. P. Hartley's Eustace and Hilda the children play at a pool among the stones of the shore

explanation.surface: A literary quiz question linking Connolly's novel with Hartley's trilogy about a brother and sister.
explanation.definitionFit: The stony seaside pool names Connolly's novel and is the setting of Hartley's opening scene with the shrimp and anemone.

clue.text: Lord Dunsany told his tales

parts.note: Dunsany's collection is called A ___'s Tales, so the teller of those tales is the person sought

explanation.surface: A remark about the Irish fantasist Lord Dunsany as a storyteller.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunsany's book title credits the stories to a visionary who sees things in sleep.

clue.text: She bore 11

parts.note: the woman who brought forth the novel given at 11, read as if she had given birth to it

explanation.surface: A woman gave birth to entry 11.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' suggests childbirth, but here means produced as a writer: the American novelist wrote A Charmed Life (1955).
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist and critic produced the 1955 novel named at 11.

clue.text: Some dramaturge, never recognized as such, becomes novelist

indicators.note: only a part of the words dramaturge never is wanted, the letters running across the gap

explanation.surface: A playwright who never got recognition turns to writing novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes letters from inside 'dramaturge, never'; 'recognized as such' and 'becomes' just link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was the Russian author of Fathers and Sons, a classic writer of fiction.

clue.text: Make short work, take up position, and resist

parts.note: op. is the short form of opus, a musical or literary work
to pose is to adopt a position, as for a portrait

explanation.surface: Instructions to be brisk, get into place and fight back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' is only a link; the pieces come in order and 'and' leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To set oneself against something is to resist it.

clue.text: Ancient king, very loud in old age

indicators.note: the musical mark for very loud is placed inside the letters for old age

parts.note: OA is an abbreviation for old age
ff, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch who was still boisterous in his dotage.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa was an eighth-century ruler of Mercia, famous for his dyke.

clue.text: He saw old ships sail like swans asleep

definitions.text: He saw old ships sail like swans asleep

parts.words: He saw old ships sail like swans asleep
parts.note: a quotation from the poem The Old Ships, which opens 'I have seen old ships sail like swans asleep', so the poet is wanted

explanation.surface: A man watched ancient vessels glide as gracefully as sleeping swans.
explanation.definitionFit: James Elroy Flecker wrote The Old Ships, whose first line describes this sight.

clue.text: Real equals, perhaps, for watercolours

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of real equals may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Paintings regarded as true peers of one another.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquarelle is a painting in transparent watercolour.

clue.text: Greyfriars boy, mature in Coppard's work

parts.note: Bob Cherry is a schoolboy at Greyfriars, the school of Billy Bunter stories
ripe means fully developed or mature

explanation.surface: A schoolboy from the Bunter stories grows up in A. E. Coppard's writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Greyfriars is the fictional English boarding school of Frank Richards's Billy Bunter stories; 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A. E. Coppard published a collection titled with this old London street cry for cherries.

clue.text: P. C. Wren's ideal boy friend?

definitions.meaning: Wren's novel of the Foreign Legion is ___ Geste, named for its hero

explanation.definitionFit: Wren's hero Michael Geste has this nickname, and the word also means a male suitor.

clue.text: A bewitched biography from 3?

parts.note: charmed means put under a spell
a life is a written account of someone's history

explanation.surface: A biography under a spell, from the writer at 3.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary McCarthy's 1955 novel bears this title.

clue.text: Caliph in new claim, amply demonstrated

indicators.note: the letters are shown openly within claim amply, running across the two words

explanation.surface: An Islamic ruler makes a fresh claim and proves it fully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' and 'in' are links here; the letters straddle 'claim' and 'amply'.
explanation.definitionFit: The caliph was the leader of Muslim prayer and of the faithful, a role named by this title.

clue.text: Eliot's weird, secret oak in Somerset

indicators.note: weird signals that the letters of secret oak are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: A strange hidden oak tree in Somerset that T. S. Eliot wrote about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Somerset' places the village; Eliot's ancestors came from there and he named one of his Four Quartets after it.
explanation.definitionFit: One of Eliot's Four Quartets takes its name from this Somerset village.

clue.text: Glorification of a vessel he holds up is so strange

parts.note: a pot is a container or vessel
taken as written

indicators.note: strange means the letters of is so are jumbled

explanation.surface: Praising a vessel that a man holds up seems odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds up' is just a link here; 'strange' makes OSIS from IS SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising someone to divine status is the highest exaltation or deification.

clue.text: Quiet boy the French made Prince of Tyre

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
Eric is a boy's name
les is the plural form of the in French

explanation.surface: A quiet French boy was crowned ruler of Tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' is a link joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play is titled after this hero, who rules Tyre.

clue.text: Hardy colaaborator is a plant

definitions.meaning: Stan ___ was the comic partner of Oliver Hardy
the bay tree, an evergreen shrub

explanation.definitionFit: Stan of the comedy duo shares his surname with the bay shrub used for victors' wreaths.

clue.text: A month in France, possibly mid roses

indicators.note: possibly signals that mid roses may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A French month, perhaps when the roses are in full bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Messidor was the harvest month of the French Revolutionary calendar, roughly June to July.

clue.text: Label base for Indian writer

parts.note: a tag is a label attached to something
ore is the base, the raw rock from which metal is won

explanation.surface: A label is found at the foot of an Indian author's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabindranath Tagore was a Bengali poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Lady responsible for spreading the news

definitions.text: Lady responsible for spreading the news

parts.words: Lady responsible for spreading the news
parts.note: Spreading the News is a one-act comedy written by an Irish noblewoman of the Abbey Theatre

explanation.surface: A woman who goes about telling everyone the gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a gossip, but Lady Augusta Gregory wrote the play Spreading the News (1904).
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Gregory, co-founder of Dublin's Abbey Theatre, wrote the play of that title.

clue.text: Familiar address to feminist sounds relevant

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word for relevant is spoken, giving a name that sounds the same

parts.note: germane means pertinent or relevant

explanation.surface: Calling a feminist by her first name seems apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Germaine Greer, author of The Female Eunuch, would be greeted by this first name by friends.

clue.text: A moment of it is sometimes worth a life's experience, thought Oliver Wendell Holmes

definitions.text: A moment of it is sometimes worth a life's experience, thought Oliver Wendell Holmes

parts.words: A moment of it is sometimes worth a life's experience, thought Oliver Wendell Holmes
parts.note: Holmes wrote that a moment's sudden understanding can be worth a lifetime of experience

explanation.surface: A quotation from Holmes about a flash of understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes's saying runs 'A moment's insight is sometimes worth a life's experience'.

clue.text: "What fates — that men must needs abide" (Henry VI, Part 3)

definitions.text: "What fates — that men must needs abide" (Henry VI, Part 3)

parts.words: "What fates — that men must needs abide" (Henry VI, Part 3)
parts.note: a fill-in quotation from Shakespeare: the missing verb is what the fates do to men that they must accept

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare's Henry VI about fate.
explanation.definitionFit: In 3 Henry VI the line runs 'What fates impose, that men must needs abide', meaning to lay on as a burden.

clue.text: Though tough and thorough, they are not sound

definitions.text: Though tough and thorough, they are not sound

parts.words: Though tough and thorough, they are not sound
parts.note: these words look alike in spelling at the end yet are said differently, so they match on paper only

explanation.surface: Something hardy and complete is nevertheless unsound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not sound' suggests faulty, but means they do not match when spoken: the endings look identical on the page only.
explanation.definitionFit: Pairs such as 'though' and 'tough' match in spelling but not pronunciation, which defines this term.

clue.text: Terry Pratchett's world, Hades to many

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and another name for it
C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many

explanation.surface: Pratchett's fantasy world seems like hell to a lot of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link joining the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Pratchett's comic fantasy novels are set on a flat world shaped like a plate, carried by elephants.

clue.text: It's in the bone, according to Robertson Davies, Grant Allen and Thomas Nelson Page

definitions.text: It's in the bone, according to Robertson Davies, Grant Allen and Thomas Nelson Page

parts.words: It's in the bone, according to Robertson Davies, Grant Allen and Thomas Nelson Page
parts.note: each of these authors used the title What's ___ in the Bone, from the proverb about inherited nature

explanation.surface: Three authors all agree something lies deep in the bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'What's bred in the bone will come out in the flesh' gives all three titles.

clue.text: Second highest punctuation mark

parts.note: top means uppermost or highest

explanation.surface: The runner-up rank among punctuation marks.
explanation.definitionFit: A full point ending a sentence is called this, as in telegrams.

clue.text: With which Fleming demonstrated the Midas touch?

definitions.text: With which Fleming demonstrated the Midas touch?

parts.words: With which Fleming demonstrated the Midas touch?
parts.note: Midas turned everything to gold with a touch, and Ian Fleming named a Bond villain after a precious-metal digit

explanation.surface: A question about how a man named Fleming showed a talent for making money.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming's 1959 Bond novel features a villain obsessed with gold, like King Midas.

clue.text: 'But I hae dream'd a dreary dream, / Beyond the Isle of —' (Chevy Chase)

parts.words: 'But I hae dream'd a dreary dream, / Beyond the Isle of —' (Chevy Chase)
parts.note: a fill-in from the Border ballad: the missing word is a Hebridean island

explanation.surface: A line from an old Scottish ballad about a gloomy dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The ballad line ends with the name of the largest island of the Inner Hebrides.

clue.text: Poet going around the East changed direction

indicators.note: the poet's name goes around the word for the East, enclosing it

parts.note: Henry Reed was an English poet, author of Naming of Parts
the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: A poet travelling round Asia turned another way.
explanation.definitionFit: To be faced a new way is to have altered one's bearing or course.
